intro.heading: ABOUT ME
intro.body: I'm Muhammad Ahmed Ashar, a web developer based in Karachi. I turn ideas into websites and applications, with close attention to how they look, how they work and how people use them.

approach.heading: APPROACH
approach.body: Good design helps people understand where they are, what they can do and what happens next.
approach.caption: A principle behind my work.

about.heading: I care about how it works, and how it feels to use.
paragraphs: I'm Muhammad Ahmed Ashar, a web developer based in Karachi. My work brings together development and a background in graphic design, so I think about the interface and the code behind it as parts of the same job.

Before choosing a platform or writing code, I want to understand what you're trying to do, who it's for and how it will be used. Those questions shape the layout, the features and the tools I work with.

I build websites, online stores and web applications. Some projects call for custom development; others need a platform that makes everyday updates straightforward. I work with both, choosing the approach around the project and the people who will manage it.

Working on logos, layouts and UI mockups has taught me to pay attention to the small decisions: how content is arranged, where the eye goes and whether an interaction feels clear. I bring that same attention to development.

I studied MERN stack development at Saylani Mass IT Training and completed a three-year diploma in Computer Information Technology. My toolkit includes custom development and CMS platforms, with the specific tools listed below.
Outside of work, I'm a Hafiz-e-Quran. The focus and consistency that took are still part of how I learn and work. I also enjoy sketching ideas and tinkering with custom keyboards.
about.closing: The details matter, from the first layout to the final interaction.

projects.title: Ahmed Ashar Portfolio (This Site)
projects.alt: Ahmed Ashar portfolio homepage with the THINK. DESIGN. DEVELOP WITH CARE. headline
projects.para: Typography, motion and interaction brought together in my own portfolio.
projects.caption: My personal portfolio site

sections.title: The overview
sections.body: A portfolio should explain the work and feel considered in its own right. This website brings selected projects, my background and a custom content studio into one place. Bold type, a warm palette and scroll-driven interactions give it its visual identity.

sections.title: The idea & goals
sections.body: The goal was to bring design and development together: present the work clearly, make the website comfortable to explore on different screens, and let content evolve without editing React components for every update.

sections.title: How I built it
sections.body:
The interface is built with React and Tailwind CSS. GSAP handles text and scroll reveals, Framer Motion powers interactive elements, and Lenis coordinates smooth scrolling. Shared theme tokens keep the public pages and dashboard connected.

A Node.js backend separates saved drafts from published content. The dashboard validates edits, previews them in a same-origin iframe and publishes to shared storage. Public pages render on the server before the browser hydrates them.

sections.title: Challenges & solutions
sections.body:
Animated text and interactive controls need clear ownership of the DOM. Wrapping the project filters in SplitText interfered with React interaction; keeping the controls outside that wrapper restored reliable mouse, keyboard and touch filtering.

Route changes introduced another subtle problem: offscreen reveals could run before the scroll position reset. Resetting Lenis in a layout effect before incoming page animations initialize fixed the revisit behavior. The dashboard uses native scrolling so forms and nested panels remain usable.

sections.title: The result
sections.body: The repository now contains a responsive portfolio, editable page content, project filters, dark and light themes, and a password-protected content studio. Publishing, image uploads, server rendering and metadata share the same content model. Browser tests cover public navigation and the isolated dashboard workflow.

sections.title: What I learned
sections.body: Small interaction details need the same attention as the layout. Testing real clicks, keyboard input, route revisits and server-rendered pages helps catch problems that a static screenshot cannot show. Keeping content validation shared between browser and server also makes the editing workflow easier to maintain.

sections.title: What's next
sections.body: The next step is to document the thinking behind each project and keep those stories editable from the studio. Analytics reporting is implemented; its live account connection still needs verification.
